content:
## Source
.design/m5/43-federation.md — REQ-7, AC-7 + decomposition PR 2.

## Surface
- New file: `polaris-backend/src/federation/state.rs` — explicit state machine.
- New file: `polaris-backend/src/repo/federation.rs` — sqlx queries for federation tables.
- New migrations:
  - `federation_peers` — peer DID + direction + trust label
  - `federation_escalations` — local view of cross-instance escalation: (id UUID PK, source_did, target_did, state, original_cid, opened_at, last_event_at)
  - `federation_messages` — append-only log of cross-instance conversation messages with signing-key DID + verification status
  - `federation_state_transitions` — append-only audit (escalation_id, from_state, to_state, triggered_by_cid, at TIMESTAMPTZ)

## State machine
States: `Proposed`, `Acknowledged`, `Active`, `Resolved`, `WithdrawnBySource`, `RejectedByTarget`.

Transitions:
- `Proposed → Acknowledged` (target ack)
- `Acknowledged → Active` (first message exchanged)
- `Active → Resolved` (either side closes)
- `Proposed → RejectedByTarget` (target rejects)
- `Proposed | Acknowledged | Active → WithdrawnBySource` (source withdraws)
- terminal states (Resolved, WithdrawnBySource, RejectedByTarget) cannot transition further.

## Rust-quality notes
- **Encode as typestate** per rust-quality §2: `Escalation<Proposed>`, `Escalation<Acknowledged>`, etc., with `impl Escalation<Proposed> { pub fn acknowledge(self) -> Escalation<Acknowledged>; }`. Compile-time impossible to skip states.
  - If typestate proves awkward across the async DB-write boundary (each transition involves a write), fall back to a runtime enum `EscalationState` with an exhaustive `match` at every transition site + a `tracing::error!` on any default arm that should be unreachable.
- **Append-only audit table** uses `INSERT … RETURNING id` and never updates. No `UPDATE` on `federation_state_transitions` — enforce with a Postgres rule or trigger.
- **No `&mut self` on transition functions** — transitions return a new typed value; the old state is consumed. (`fn acknowledge(self) -> …`)
- All state transitions emit a `tracing::info_span!` with `escalation_id = %id, from_state = %from, to_state = %to` so operators can grep audit logs by escalation_id (REQ-7).
- The `materialize_from_quarantine` function reads `federation_quarantine` (from PR 1), validates the wire shape via `polaris_lexicons::Escalation::deserialize`, allocates a `federation_escalations` row, walks the state machine, and deletes the quarantine row in a single SQL transaction.

## External references
- typestate pattern: https://www.lurklurk.org/effective-rust/typestate.html
- sqlx transaction docs: https://docs.rs/sqlx/latest/sqlx/struct.Transaction.html

## Acceptance (AC-7)
- [ ] Network partition test: drop the WebSocket between A and B mid-Active state; reconnect; verify both sides resume at last-known-good state (no duplicate transitions in `federation_state_transitions`).
- [ ] Property test (proptest): generate random valid transition sequences, assert the state machine never enters an unreachable state.
- [ ] Migration round-trips: `cargo sqlx migrate run` on a fresh DB succeeds; sqlx offline cache regenerates without diff.
